restatement: A CASE branch has to accept more than one quoted value. A WHEN can hold a comma-separated list of literals and variable paths, one variable, or one comparison (== != > < >= <=). Equality uses the operators card rule (valuesEqual): quoted text compares as text, unquoted numbers compare as numbers. The ordered operators use evaluateNumericComparison, and a non-numeric side is a type-error located at the WHEN. A missing variable follows strict mode. A malformed WHEN is a syntax-error at the tag, raised at parse time in render, validate and analyze. analyze records WHEN paths as case usage. render and resolveTemplate behave the same. Existing CASE behavior stays. The work must not change existing test expectations, add a dependency, evaluate template text or compile template regexes, or let unknown names pass in lenient mode.
brief_mismatch: Two problems in the brief. First, the spec's Interface section and the card's Interface contract require a golden case folder tests/golden/render-cases/lang-case/ with template.md, data.json and expected.md, but files_scope lists only template.md. The manifest amendment then drops template.md as already committed before the base, so no part of the golden case is in this card's scope or in the diff. Second, the card's must-not allows 'one named amendment (if any)' to the test expectations, while the packet's m1 forbids changing any existing test expectation. No amendment is named anywhere.
verification_plan: c1: a list of quoted values matches either value. Check commas inside quotes, spacing, single and double quotes, the first matching WHEN winning, and DEFAULT when nothing matches.

c2: a variable matcher is read with the same lookup as the subject (loop names, @ names, paths, hyphenated names). A strict missing variable is missing-variable at the WHEN; lenient reads empty text. A variable counts as unquoted for equality.

c3: all six operators work. != is the negation of ==. The ordered operators go through evaluateNumericComparison. Non-numeric, empty, missing, null, cyclic or BigInt operands give a located type-error, never a raw exception.
c4: every malformed form from the spec is a syntax-error at the WHEN line and column in render, validate and analyze, including in branches that never render.
c5: analyze records path items from both list and comparison forms as case usage, not optional. It excludes literals, loop names and @ names, and agrees with what strict render reports missing.
Existing behavior: WHEN "" still matches a missing or null subject, the old single quoted form matches as before, WhenNode.value is kept, and CASE subject errors are unchanged.
No copies of the equality or numeric helpers, and one shared quote-aware comma scanner.
m1: compare the frozen tests with the diff for any changed expectation.
m2/m3: no new imports from packages, and no RegExp built from template text.
m4: unknown names and malformed items are errors in lenient mode too.
Scope: the diff touches only the files in the manifest, and the golden case exists and runs.

findings.title: The builder changed the frozen case test: one expectation flipped, one assertion loosened, lowercase cases deleted

serves.scenario: tests/language/case.test.ts was committed by the test writer before the base (diff index cefd7ff..1df683a). It is the frozen contract for this card. The diff changes the lenient expectation for WHEN "a" ; other with {x:"b"} from O("2") to O("D"). It loosens the cs-analyze 'exactly the expected variables' assertion to ignore x and items. It deletes the lowercase-tag cases. The new expectation matches the spec: a lenient missing variable is empty text, and "b" does not equal "". But the test now encodes what the builder chose rather than what the plan fixed, and no approved amendment covers it. The scope exceptions log lists only the spec.md wording change, not this test file.

findings.title: WHEN_PATH accepts names the language does not treat as names, such as n-1, a-, a--b and @ inside a name

serves.scenario: The language contract says a hyphen joins a name only between two ASCII letters; n-1, x1-y and 1-a are arithmetic. The new WHEN_PATH regex /^[\p{L}_@][\p{L}\p{N}_@-]*(\.[\p{L}\p{N}_@-]+)*$/u accepts limit-1, a-, a--b and a@b as variable paths. It is a second name rule, separate from the parser's VARIABLE_PATH. An author who writes {{WHEN limit-1}} gets no syntax-error at parse. In lenient mode the item reads as a missing variable, which is empty text, so the CASE silently takes the wrong branch. analyze also reports a required variable 'limit-1'. Under ADR 0003 an item that is neither a literal nor a variable path must be an error in every mode.

findings.rubric: unknown names, operators and filters are still errors in every mode
findings.reproduction: render('{{CASE x}}{{WHEN limit-1}}Y{{DEFAULT}}N{{END_CASE}}', {x:'', limit:5}, {strictMode:false}). Expected per the contract: a syntax-error at 1:11. Observed by reading the code: ok, output 'Y', because limit-1 is read as an empty missing variable and equals the empty subject. analyze on the same template lists 'limit-1'.

findings.title: A quoted WHEN value ending in a backslash, which worked before, is now an unclosed-quote syntax-error

serves.scenario: The spec says the old single form keeps matching text exactly as before and that a quoted text is not unescaped. splitCommas treats a quote preceded by a backslash as still open (text[i-1] !== '\\'). At the base, {{WHEN 'C:\'}} matched the text C:\ through the old regex. At head it fails with 'Unclosed quote in {{WHEN}}', so a template that used to render now stops with an error. The scanner thereby treats a backslash before a quote as an escape, which contradicts the spec's no-unescape rule for WHEN.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: render("{{CASE p}}{{WHEN 'C:\\'}}Y{{DEFAULT}}N{{END_CASE}}", {p:'C:\\'}). At base f140e131 the output is 'Y'. At head the result is a syntax-error at the WHEN. No test covers a trailing backslash inside quotes.
